general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **US/China/Semiconductors:** US Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo announced a total ban on the export of 2nm chip-making equipment to China effective November 14, 2026. This policy follows a verified breach of existing export licenses by three semiconductor firms based in Shenzhen. Beijing's Ministry of Commerce responded by imposing a retaliatory export quota on gallium and germanium, reducing shipments to the US by 40% starting Monday. This escalates the "chip war," threatening global supply chains for high-end computing and AI hardware. Reuters

• **EU/Namibia/Energy:** The European Commission and the government of Namibia signed a €12 billion Green Hydrogen Partnership on November 14, 2026, to construct four electrolysis plants in the Erongo region. The agreement mandates that 60% of the hydrogen produced will be exported to Germany and the Netherlands via the Port of Walvis Bay. The Namibia Stock Exchange saw energy-related shares rise by 8% following the announcement. This signals a strategic shift in the EU's energy diversification to reduce reliance on volatile fossil fuel imports. Financial Times

• **International AI Governance:** Leaders from 45 countries, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and the US President, signed the Geneva AI Safety Accord on November 14, 2026. The treaty establishes a mandatory "kill-switch" protocol for any AI model exceeding $10^{26}$ floating-point operations (FLOPs) of compute. Three major AI laboratories in San Francisco and Beijing agreed to submit their training logs to the newly formed International AI Agency (IAIA) for immediate audit. This creates the first legally binding international framework to prevent catastrophic AI risks, directly impacting the deployment schedules of frontier models. AP

• **Saudi Arabia/Iran/Diplomacy:** The governments of Saudi Arabia and Iran finalized a comprehensive Security Pact in Riyadh on November 14, 2026, ending a decade of proxy conflicts in Yemen. The agreement includes a mutual non-interference clause and the establishment of a joint maritime security task force to patrol the Red Sea. The UN Security Council passed Resolution 2841 by a vote of 14-0 to formally recognize the pact and authorize a reduction in international monitoring forces. This stabilization of the Gulf reduces the geopolitical risk premium on crude oil prices and alters the strategic balance of power in the Middle East. Al Jazeera

Why it matters: The simultaneous shift toward restrictive tech trade, new green energy dependencies, and high-level diplomatic stabilization indicates a global transition toward a fragmented, bloc-based world order.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **AI Act (High-Risk AI Systems):** Providers of high-risk AI systems (e.g., those used in recruitment, credit scoring, or critical infrastructure) must now implement a mandatory quality management system and technical documentation for CE marking. Previously: No EU-wide mandatory certification for high-risk AI. Now: Mandatory conformity assessments and registration in the EU database are required before market placement. Compliance deadline: Immediate for systems placed on the market after August 2026. Impact: Increases operational and legal compliance costs for Portuguese tech startups scaling AI products in the EU. [EUR-Lex]

• **Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Definitive Period):** Importers of carbon-intensive goods (steel, aluminum, cement, electricity, and hydrogen) are now required to purchase and surrender CBAM certificates to cover embedded emissions. Previously: Transitional period (ending December 31, 2025) required only quarterly reporting without payment. Now: Mandatory financial payments tied to the weekly average auction price of EU ETS allowances. Compliance deadline: First full annual surrender of certificates by May 31, 2027, for 2026 imports. Impact: Direct increase in procurement costs for Portuguese industrial importers of raw materials. [European Commission]

• **Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD - Large Undertakings):** All companies meeting at least two of three criteria—>250 employees, >€50m net turnover, or >€25m total assets—must now report sustainability data according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Previously: Only NFRD-scope companies (>500 employees) were mandated to report. Now: Scope expanded to include all large enterprises, requiring third-party limited assurance. Compliance deadline: Annual reports for the 2025 financial year must be published by mid-2026. Impact: Significant increase in audit and accounting overhead for medium-to-large Portuguese firms. [EUR-Lex]

• **MiCA Delegated Regulation (CASP Capital Requirements):** Crypto-Asset Service Providers (CASPs) must maintain own-funds equal to the higher of €150,000 or one-quarter of the fixed overheads from the preceding year. Previously: Fragmented national capital requirements across EU member states. Now: Uniform minimum capital requirements for all licensed CASPs operating within the Union. Compliance deadline: November 1, 2026. Impact: May trigger consolidation of smaller Portuguese crypto-asset firms unable to meet these liquidity thresholds. [Official Journal of the EU]

Why it matters: The EU has shifted from "reporting phases" to "payment and certification phases" across climate, AI, and finance, creating immediate financial liabilities for importers and tech providers.
